sections.title: Date and Time of Discharge
sections.promptHint: Doctor enters manually when starting the draft; DisDate in the system is empty until the hospital finalizes discharge.

sections.title: Diagnosis
sections.promptHint: List the primary dermatological diagnosis first, then secondaries. Use exact clinical wording; do not add or reclassify diagnoses.

sections.title: Presenting Complaints
sections.promptHint: Summarize distinct complaints of type 'Chief Complaint' only. Collapse repeated rows with the same complaint into one clean line, adding the recorded date or date range when useful. Preserve the recorded skin-related wording; do not include associated complaints or dump raw rows. Return one item per line; do not leave an escaped-newline marker visible in the text.

sections.title: History of Present Illness
sections.promptHint: Write a concise chronological History of Present Illness using the chief complaints plus associated complaints and recorded remarks, emphasizing the documented evolution of skin findings, onset, distribution, itching, and treatments tried. Group repeated symptoms rather than listing every row. Use only this recorded proxy, do not invent detail, and do not replace the narrative with a disclaimer. Add at most one short review caveat at the end if needed.

sections.title: Past Medical History
sections.promptHint: Summarize the distinct recorded problems as a concise Past Medical History, including status, onset, comorbidity, and prior dermatological conditions such as eczema when present. Treat problems not obviously tied to the current admission diagnosis as past history, but do not invent or reclassify conditions. Write the useful list first; add at most one short review caveat at the end if needed.

sections.title: Current Medication
sections.promptHint: Only orders with status ACTIVE, including topical treatments and emollients. Source does not separate home from admission-started medications; treat as best effort.

sections.title: Personal History
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent habits or lifestyle detail.

sections.title: Family History
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent family history of atopy or psoriasis.

sections.title: Allergies
sections.promptHint: List each allergen with reaction nature and symptoms — drug allergies matter for future dermatological prescribing — or state the recorded status (e.g. NKA).

sections.title: Occupational History
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent occupational or irritant-exposure detail.

sections.title: On Examination
sections.promptHint: Most recent vitals only, and state explicitly this covers recorded vitals, not a skin examination. Where skin findings are mentioned they must come only from recorded complaints and notes; do not invent morphology, distribution, or erythema descriptors.

sections.title: Course in Hospital
sections.promptHint: Synthesize notes, labs, radiology, medication changes, and the vitals trend, emphasizing skin-directed therapy started or stopped during the stay (topicals, systemic agents) and any recorded fever or infection markers that drove changes. Do not reproduce a medication list here; medication sections are canonical. Stick strictly to the data; doctor review required.

sections.title: Condition at Discharge
sections.promptHint: Most recent vitals plus current status of active problems. Report recorded values; do not overstate skin improvement without recorded evidence.

sections.title: Medications During Stay
sections.promptHint: Orders with a start_date inside the admission window, including completed and discontinued ones with stop dates.

sections.title: Medications on Discharge
sections.promptHint: Only orders with status ACTIVE at draft time, including topicals and emollients with their schedules.

sections.title: Advice
sections.promptHint: No structured source. May draft generic advice grounded only in the recorded dermatological diagnoses (e.g. continue emollients as recorded); flagged as needing doctor review.

sections.title: Special Needs
sections.promptHint: No source in the API. Leave blank for the doctor; never invent care needs.

sections.title: Follow Up Advice
sections.promptHint: No structured source. May draft generic dermatology follow-up advice grounded only in the diagnoses; flagged as needing doctor review.
